Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopNova Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing up questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopNova Inc.'s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are David Liang, CEO; Emily Harper, CFO; Michael Ruiz, COO; Lisa Wong, CMO; and Raj Singh, CTO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Liang, CEO of ShopNova Inc.

David Liang:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by accelerating international market expansion and robust advertising efficiencies. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV and active users across our global platform.

Our focus remains on new product launches and operational resilience amid macroeconomic pressures. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our SphereAI Personal Shopper and SphereFresh Unlimited, which we believe will significantly enhance conversion rates and customer lifetime value.

We are investing heavily in supply chain enhancements and technology enablers to support seasonality trends and revenue acceleration.

We are focused on improving ROAS through data-driven optimizations and expanding into high-growth regions.

Finally, we are committed to delivering shareholder value through disciplined growth and marketplace scale.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Emily Harper, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Emily Harper:
Thank you, David. Our Q2 revenue was $30.1 billion, an increase of 14.2% year-over-year and 7.8% quarter-over-quarter. This beat our prior guidance of $28.0 to $29.0 billion by 6% at the midpoint, reflecting the strength of our diversified revenue streams, deeper customer penetration, and accelerating monetization. Gross margin was 38.5%, driven by improved take rates, supply chain efficiencies, and private label expansion. Operating expenses were $6.8 billion, representing 22.6% of revenue. Our marketing spend remained disciplined at 22% of revenue, down from 25% last year, thanks to strong ROAS performance.

Let me dive deeper into revenue growth. Q2 revenue hit $30.1 billion, up 14.2% YoY from $26.3 billion and 7.8% QoQ from $27.9 billion in Q1. This marks our 11th straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth. By segment, retail marketplace revenue at $20.2 billion grew 16.5% YoY, fueled by $85.4 billion in GMV, up 18%, with AI-powered recommendations boosting conversions by 28%. Advertising and services contributed $6.6 billion, up 12.8%, while subscriptions hit $3.3 billion, up 8.7%, with NexPrime-like memberships at 185 million subs and low churn.

Regionally, North America drove $17.5 billion, up 15.8%; EMEA $6.6 billion, up 13.2%; APAC $4.5 billion, up 18.4%; and Latin America $1.5 billion, up 9.1%. Inventory turns improved to 12.5x, dynamic pricing captured margin expansion, and our repeat purchase rate held at 85%.

Turning to international market expansion, one of our key growth engines. We've been scaling aggressively since our 2022 global pivot, targeting the $6.5 trillion e-commerce opportunity. In Q2, international GMV reached $1.2 billion, up 68% YoY and 32% of total GMV, accelerating from 24% last year. International revenue hit $285 million, up 72% YoY and 28% of total, driving 45% of top-line growth. Active sellers grew 55% to 45,000, buyers to 18 million MAUs, up 62%, with ARPU at $28, up 14%.

In APAC, 52% of international GMV at $624 million, up 92%, with India at $210 million, up 115%, via UPI and local wallets boosting conversions to 4.2%. Southeast Asia ARPU at $35 on premium electronics. Europe GMV $380 million, up 42%, with UK and Germany leading post-VAT compliance, EuroFlash program cutting costs 22%. Latin America doubled to $145 million, Brazil up 140% with Mercado Libre partnerships and Pix payments. Other regions added $51 million.

We've invested $45 million YTD in GlobalEdge platform supporting 14 languages, reducing abandonment 19%. Capex of $120 million for new centers aims for 85% sub-3-day delivery. We expect 60-70% international GMV growth FY24, mix to 38%.

On advertising and marketing spend efficiency, our blended ROAS was 5.8x, up 12% YoY from 5.2x, generating $1.2 billion ad-attributed GMV on $207 million spend, outperforming industry 4.2-4.8x. By channel: search 8.2x with Performance Max; social/video 4.9x, TikTok 7.4x; display/retail media 4.1x, our network at 12x; emerging CTV 3.2x. North America 6.4x, EMEA 4.7x, APAC 4.2x. Underpinned by MaxBid AI lifting ROAS 25%, creative testing, and LTV focus. Q3 ROAS 6.0-6.3x expected.

Macroeconomic factors impacted GMV and revenue, but we showed resilience with $85.4 billion GMV up 18% and revenue up 14.2%. Inflation at 5.2% CPI drove value-seeking, boosting private labels 18%, but AOV down 8% in discretionary. Higher rates curbed big-ticket, U.S. GMV moderated to 9% in some areas. North America resilient at 11%, Europe flat amid energy crisis, APAC up 28%, LATAM 16%. Mitigated by AI forecasting reducing obsolescence 23%, EdgeLogistics saving $180 million, personalization lifting repeats 7%. Defensive levers: essentials to 35% GMV, 150,000 new SMBs.

On new product launches, SphereAI Personal Shopper drove 28% conversion lift, 17% AOV to $145, $1.2 billion GMV, NPS 78. SphereFresh Unlimited added 450,000 subs, 8% grocery GMV penetration. LiveSphere generated $350 million GMV at 12% conversions. Lowering CAC 22%, $250 million more investment planned.

Finally, seasonality: Q2 at 21% of YTD GMV, up 8% YoY, compressing troughs. Q4 typically 42-48%, but deviations from macro and supply issues softened it slightly; countered by NovaAI, same-day delivery lifting Q2 15%. Smoothing with subscriptions, projecting 14/22/23/41% FY24.

Our net income for the quarter was $2.1 billion, or $1.85 per share. We ended with $15.4 billion in cash and equivalents. We are reaffirming full-year guidance of $122-126 billion revenue, 13-16% growth.

Now I'll turn it over to Michael Ruiz to discuss operations.

Michael Ruiz:
Thanks, Emily. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and fulfillment network expansion. Our shipping times improved by 22%, with sub-3-day coverage at 85% in key markets. Fulfillment costs improved 18% to 11% of GMV through AI route optimization and DHL partnerships. We are implementing GlobalEdge enhancements and micro-fulfillment centers in Leipzig, Milan, Singapore, and São Paulo.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa Wong.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, Michael. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns and TikTok Shop integrations, alongside Performance Max and Demand Gen. Customer acquisition costs held at $22, with payback under 4 months. Our brand awareness increased by 25%, measured by LTV/CAC at 4.2x. We are focusing on retail media network growth and GenAI bidding for sustained ROAS above 5x.

Now I'll turn it over to Raj Singh.

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Lisa. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization and cookieless tracking migrations. Our website uptime was 99.98%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%, now 62% of orders. We're investing in TensorFlow-based engines, server-side tagging with LiveRamp, and Web3 loyalty pilots.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A: Please press star then 1 to queue. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Emily, could you expand on the revenue beat versus guidance? What were the key surprises in segments and regions?

David Liang:
Thanks, Ben. The beat was broad-based, but marketplace revenue exceeded with 18% GMV growth from new customers and AI recs. APAC accelerated beyond expectations at 18.4%, while ads hit take rates ahead of plan. We're seeing early signs of seasonality compression helping Q2 ramp.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Priya Patel:
Great, thanks. On international expansion, Emily or David, the APAC numbers look impressive—India 115% growth. Any updates on logistics challenges and FY24 outlook?

Emily Harper:
Hi Priya. Yes, India GMV to $210 million via UPI and hyper-local storefronts. Logistics improving with Flipkart partnerships for same-day in Tier-2 cities. LATAM fulfillment at 15% but DHL targeting sub-5-day. Still 60-70% growth FY24, mix to 38%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with JPMorgan.

Alex Kim:
Thanks. Michael, operations-wise, how are you addressing fulfillment costs in emerging markets, and any color on new center capex?

Michael Ruiz:
Absolutely, Alex. Costs higher in LATAM at 15% versus global 11%, but DHL eCommerce and new hubs like Mexico City and São Paulo will drive down to 12% by year-end. $120 million capex focused there, enabling 85% coverage.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with Barclays.

Jordan Lee:
Lisa, marketing spend efficiency—ROAS at 5.8x is strong. Breakdown by region and any TikTok risks?

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, Jordan. Blended 5.8x, with TikTok at 7.4x despite scrutiny, offset by Meta and search. APAC challenged but pilots countering. Retail media at 12x ROAS helping keep marketing at 22% of revenue.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with Citi.

Taylor Brooks:
Emily, on macro impacts and seasonality deviations—how are you positioning for Q3 with inflation and rates?

Emily Harper:
Good question, Taylor. Inflation drove value shift, but personalization and essentials mix mitigated AOV drop. Seasonality flattening with subscriptions stabilizing Q1 troughs. Q3 GMV 10-13%, revenue 12-15%, factoring recession risks but APAC tailwinds.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to David Liang for closing remarks.

David Liang:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders—leveraging international scale, tech innovations like SphereAI, and marketing discipline amid macro resilience. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
